 Mumbai, October 29: Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Thursday, October 29. Petrol costs Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi, Rs 111.21 in Mumbai and Rs 113.51 in Kolkata, while diesel is priced at Rs 95.20 per litre in Delhi, Rs 97.83 in Mumbai and Rs 99.82 in Kolkata. Among the listed cities, Hyderabad and Thiruvananthapuram have some of the highest fuel prices, while Chandigarh records the lowest diesel rate at Rs 89.47 per litre.    
 Oil prices fell on Thursday as hopes of renewed diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran eased concerns over potential supply disruptions, although escalating attacks in the Middle East limited the decline. Brent crude futures dropped 1% to $114.2 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 1.4% to $101.4. Both benchmarks had risen in the previous session, with Brent gaining 1.3% and WTI climbing 3%.    
 Selling pressure followed reports that US Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei seeking to revive peace negotiations. Qatar has also presented Tehran with a draft proposal to end the US-Israeli war, but an Iranian official dismissed the terms as unacceptable. Market participants remain cautious about whether diplomatic efforts can prevent a further escalation of the conflict.    
 Supply concerns continued to underpin prices as Houthi attacks intensified across the region. Yemen’s Houthis reportedly attacked Aden airport, while the group also claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, a facility with a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. Saudi authorities had not confirmed the refinery attack. Investors are also weighing the risk of possible US military action against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections.    
 Separately, US crude inventories fell by 1.9 million barrels in the week ended October 23, against analysts’ expectations for a marginal increase, according to the US Energy Information Administration. However, gasoline stockpiles rose by 3.9 million barrels, compared with forecasts for a decline. For India, where crude imports account for a substantial share of energy requirements, oil prices remain a key variable for inflation, the import bill, the rupee and corporate profitability.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel rates in your city.  
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian metro cities and state capitals, with Delhi retailing fuel at Rs 102.12 per litre on Thursday. In neighbouring Noida, petrol was priced at Rs 101.96 per litre, while Gurgaon recorded a rate of Rs 102.97 per litre. Chandigarh had one of the lowest prices among the listed cities, at Rs 101.54 per litre.   
 Among the major metros, Mumbai continued to have a higher petrol price at Rs 111.21 per litre, compared with Rs 113.51 in Kolkata. Chennai’s petrol price stood at Rs 107.76 per litre, while Bengaluru recorded Rs 111.68 per litre. None of these cities reported a change in rates.   
 Among other state capitals, Jaipur sold petrol at Rs 113.19 per litre and Patna at Rs 113.37 per litre. Hyderabad recorded one of the highest rates at Rs 116.15 per litre, followed by Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 115.49 per litre. Bhubaneswar’s petrol price stood at Rs 108.97 per litre.   
 In Lucknow, petrol was priced at Rs 101.86 per litre, while the rate in Chandigarh remained at Rs 101.54 per litre. All listed cities reported zero price changes, indicating that retail petrol rates were stable on the day. Prices can vary across cities because of differences in state taxes, local levies and transportation costs.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian metro cities and state capitals on Thursday, with Delhi retailing the fuel at Rs 95.20 per litre. In neighbouring Noida, diesel was priced at Rs 95.44 per litre, while Gurgaon recorded a rate of Rs 95.64 per litre. Chandigarh had the lowest diesel price among the listed cities, at Rs 89.47 per litre.   
 Among the major metros, diesel cost Rs 97.83 per litre in Mumbai and Rs 99.82 per litre in Kolkata. Chennai recorded a price of Rs 99.55 per litre, while Bengaluru sold diesel at Rs 99.56 per litre. Prices remained steady across all four cities, with no changes reported.   
 Among other state capitals, diesel was priced at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 98.25 per litre in Jaipur. Patna recorded a rate of Rs 99.36 per litre, while Lucknow sold diesel at Rs 95.36 per litre. Hyderabad and Thiruvananthapuram reported some of the highest prices, at Rs 104.23 and Rs 104.40 per litre, respectively.   
 Diesel prices registered no change across any of the listed cities, indicating stability in retail fuel rates on the day. Differences in prices across locations largely reflect variations in state taxes, local levies and transportation costs.
